name: Nick Saraev
inspiration: instagram.com/nick_saraev — the 'white gallery' reel. Refs pulled from his last 10 reels (Jul 30 - Aug 17 2026: DcJTgNZv3nW, DcEFABnvBuH, Db_H8ScP5y-, Db52rxbPh6i, Db3UttuvfwN, Db0zoZMPMCV, DbyJNRdPyCj, Dbvkxq3SAE0, Dbn6ElTvw_W, DblTPmfPCpB). Hard-white gallery and full-black stages, serif-italic-CAPS shock words stamped full frame, bold lowercase running captions, a coral pixel-art robot mascot that bobs between shots, and THE gesture: a REAL screenshot blurred everywhere except one sharp zone ringed by a thick neon stroke (orange/lime/cyan/red, one at a time). Real captures as evidence — never redrawn. Fastest style in the library. Reference frames in references/.
summary: The rapid-fire 'tool news' reel style. Use for 30-57s vertical announcements — someone shipped X, here is the proof, comment the keyword. One idea per shot, ~26 cuts/min, nearly twice Nathan Hodgson's pace. PLAYBOOK.md is the full A-to-Z edit recipe (beat-map table, web asset sourcing via insert-broll, zero-dead-frame QC) with a real reel decomposed shot by shot.
format: vertical reels 9:16 (1080x1920). Not built for long-form.

palette.notes: White is HARD (#FCFCFC), never cream — warming it slides into Nathan Hodgson. Coral is the only permanent accent (mascot + script voice). Neons are a rotation system for annotation frames: ONE on screen at a time, color may change shot to shot. Sampled per-pixel from the refs. Mirrored in tokens.css.

fonts.notes: The clash between voice 1 and 2 IS the style. Voice 1: serif ITALIC CAPS (Playfair 700i) for shock words, 1-3 words max, stamped full frame. Voice 2: bold lowercase geometric (Poppins 700) for running captions, 2-4 words. Voice 3: coral/white italic script for connectives, overlapping the other voice (the outro signature). Mono appears only INSIDE real captures.

motion: One speed: FAST. Everything enters in 0.22-0.30s and the cut lands before it settles. WHIP-SCALE for captures (1.12 → 1.0), STAMP for serif words (0.94 → 1.0, dry), BOB for the pixel mascot (±4° sine loop). The neon frame draws its stroke around the perimeter in ~0.4s after a beat on the full sharp page. Zoom is always still moving at the cut. No fades anywhere.
transitions: Hard cuts only, ping-ponging between the white gallery and the full-black stage several times per reel. Face returns for 1-2s breaths (cut-out on a rounded plate) between proofs. Outro is typography over the last face shot — no panel, no card.

pacing.notes: Measured across the 10 reels (scene>0.25 detection); fastest reel hits 35.5 cpm with a 1.4s median. One idea per shot — if a shot must carry two, split it. If a shot must hold >3s, this is the wrong style.

cards.notes: The shock word, full frame: serif italic CAPS, stamped dry (scale 0.94→1.0, 0.22s), holds 0.8-1.5s. theme slot = 'white' or 'black'. Chain them against captures: A FREE → screenshot → UNCENSORED → screenshot. Never more than 3 words.

THE gesture. Real screenshot arrives sharp (whip 1.12→1.0), beat ~0.6s, then everything blurs and darkens EXCEPT one zone ringed by an 8px neon stroke (radius 28) that draws around the perimeter. Zone via --rx/--ry/--rw/--rh percents. neon slot picks the color: orange | lime | cyan | red. No label — the frame alone. One neon on screen at a time.

For talking about TEXT: three centered roman-serif lines, then editor corrections slam onto them one by one — red wash behind the offending phrase, strikethrough, red pill label at the end of a leader line (UNNECESSARY INTRO / EM DASH / FAKE INSIGHT). The text never moves; only annotations pop.
The coral pixel robot (crisp cells, never smoothed) bobbing ±4° with a sine hop, alone on white or above a prop. The recurring character that stitches the reel together. theme = 'white' or 'black'.
The breath between proofs: cut-out talking head on a rounded plate (radius 64) sliding up from the bottom, bold lowercase caption over the chin. 1-2s max.

The workhorse — makes 'every element shown with an animation' reproducible. Takes ANY fetched asset (site screenshot, GitHub page, logo, product UI from insert-broll) and slams it in with one of five entrances + continuous drift until the cut: whip (default), zoomin, zoomout, pan, pop (logos/cards on stage with shadow, fit=contain). Alternate variants; never show a static asset. See PLAYBOOK.md law 3.

The outro: 'comment' in white italic script overlapping the quoted keyword in heavy bold beneath it, soft drop shadow, over the final face shot. No panel, no pill — the exact inverse of Nathan Hodgson's violet card.
